title: WebSec Campaign Plan
description: The contract between strategy and execution: the planner (LLM) proposes prioritized questions with trajectories and budgets; the deterministic orchestrator decides whether/when/where each stage runs. The plan is data, never a script the model executes.

required_context.description: artifact ids the specialist pass must be given

budget_class.description: cheap = local/static, standard = mid model, expensive = frontier model

closed_reason.description: WHY the priority was closed — required by the CLI for any closing status; 'answered' with no reason or evidence ref is the run-2 hole (Q-004 closed with a sentence instead of a probe)

closed_ref.description: evidence the closure rests on: a finding id (F-...), exec id (EXEC-...), artifact id, or file#L anchor. An 'answered' priority with no closed_ref is flagged in the report's answer-quality section

interim.description: FIX-5: the deferred-consequence statement pricing the interim window of a tier-0 row anchored on asserter — must cite a symbol from the row's own surface entry

interim_finding.description: FIX-5: the filed finding id that records the interim window of a tier-0 row anchored on asserter

probe.description: the mechanical candidate row this priority was emitted from (A3). row_id is the idempotency key; shape_sha detects a changed anchor tuple, which is the only thing that may reopen a dispositioned row; surface_sha is the index_sha the surface was built from

probe_id.description: the registered probe that produced the row; the probe_surface schema pins the enum

surface_sha.description: index_sha of the surface this row was emitted from

risk_band.description: the probe rank band the numeric risk was mapped from

anchor.description: the disposition anchor a probe-row closure cites: the field name from the probe's own anchor enum, its REAL value on the row (probes.row_anchor_value), and the rendered file#L/value citation the closure records as closed_ref. Rejected when the field is outside the probe's enum, so a disposition cannot name a part the probe never produced.

families.description: candidate families seeded from the model — the checklist a closure must attest against

families_checked.description: families the operator attested as compared/checked when closing

symmetry.description: primitive-symmetry (L-04) only: the asset-flow pairing per family member — the primitive each sibling uses to move the asset

primitives.description: the token-movement primitive(s) quoted from source, e.g. burn / safeTransfer / mint

reconciliation.description: FIX-6: the divergence reconciliation a primitive-symmetry (L-04) closure attests — one entry per funding-mismatch / member-disagreement surface row, each a per-member funding cite or a filed finding id

cites.description: per-member funding cites: primitive:Symbol#L<line> — primitive from the matrix vocabulary (burn, mint, send-native, transfer-in, transfer-out); Symbol must appear on the row's own surface entry

finding.description: the filed finding id the divergence is attached to (the other legal exit)

trajectory_matrix.description: enforces orthogonality: each trajectory gets its own perspective contract, and thin-coverage components get re-pointed

A-code.description: implementation-centric: bugs in the code as written

B-economic.description: assume the protocol is economically exploitable; find the imbalance

C-state-machine.description: find dangerous call/state sequences and illegal transitions

D-attacker.description: assume the attacker holds each realistic role; find role-abuse

E-historical.description: find variants of known exploits, patches and disclosures

F-integration.description: assume every external contract/token behaves unexpectedly

G-drift.description: spec vs implementation vs deployment vs config divergence

H-lifecycle.description: consensus/lifecycle game: the adversary WINNING the commit→challenge→finalize game
